images.caption: Figure 1:Generative VLMs vs. Decision-Native VLMs.Conventional generative VLMs are designed for open-ended reasoning and report generation, yet often rely on ungrounded visual context and yield uncalibrated confidence.Radevis a decision-native model tailored for structured, organ-grounded, and confidence-aware clinical judgment.

Figure 2:Framework of the proposed Radev.(a) The Organ-Grounded Visual Encoder uses organ masks and learned mask queries to extract 3D organ tokens. Question-selected organ tokens attend to 2D slice features within their anatomical bounds. The language backbone and candidate scoring head predict an answer distribution in a single forward pass. (b) Training proceeds through projector–evidence alignment, verdict fine-tuning, and Counterfactual-Calibrated Training (CCT). (c) CCT constructs factual, target-ablated, control-ablated, and evidence-blind views by intervening on visual features. The first three views receive task supervision, while the evidence-blind view receives a confidence-margin penalty.

Figure 4:Accuracy under confidence-based rejection.Samples are rejected in ascending order of predictive confidence. The rejection rate is the percentage of all samples rejected, and accuracy is computed over the retained samples.

Figure A1:Overview ofCT-Verdict.(a)Benchmark construction process: radiology reports are parsed into
structured findings; synthesis rules over presence,
attributes, and relations turn each finding into candidate questions; questions are generated deterministically and their labels verified by three LLM
readers with human spot-checking; finally, a
study-level split separates training from test.(b)Examples of the three question types: binary presence (noul),
multi-way choice, and ordinal severity (score).(c)Details of dataset: distributions of question types and clinical
tasks, dataset splits, and organ/disease coverage.

Figure A2:Qualitative verdicts on CT-Verdict-IID and CT-Verdict-OOD.Each row shows one axial slice, the full dataset question with its gold
label, and the verdicts of GPT-5.4 (free-text), Jev-1.14 (likelihood head),
and Radev-2B (ours). Rows (a) and (b) are successes of Radev on IID and OOD
respectively; row (c) is a failure shared by all three models, on which
Radev reports the lowest confidence.
